name: Memobase
ontology_notes: User-profile backend. Built-in slots such as basic_info/name, basic_info/gender, education/school. Configurable topic/subtopic slots in config.yaml (additional_user_profiles or overwrite_user_profiles). Events hold summary, optional tags, profile delta, created time. Blobs are ChatBlob and SummaryBlob. No character autobiography or relationship-state type. Roleplay is documented as mapping one app user to many Memobase user ids.

ontology.evidence: docs features/profile/profile.md topic/subtopic slots. features/event/event.md Event Summary, Event Tags, Profile Delta, Created Time. API users, profiles, events, blobs.
ontology.label: measured

write_policy.evidence: App inserts ChatBlob. Buffer flush (auto size/idle or flush API) runs LLM extract into profile slots. profile_validate_mode default true drops low-quality extracts. profile_strict_mode can forbid extra subtopics. Manual add/update/delete profile APIs exist.
write_policy.label: measured

read_policy.evidence: user.context() returns a formatted always-on Memory block (profile plus latest events). Optional chats= semantic/LLM ranking of events and profiles. max_tokens, prefer_topics, only_topics, time_range_in_days. Default template says not to mention memories unless relevant.
read_policy.label: measured

supersession.evidence: Profile slots are updated over time (profile evolution). max_pre_profile_token_size triggers re-summary of a slot. Events keep a profile delta history. Not a full invalidate-with-time graph.
supersession.label: measured

temporal.evidence: Events have Created Time. Message created_at is documented in practices/tips.md. context(time_range_in_days=) filters events. No last-Tuesday natural-language parser documented.
temporal.label: measured

identity_split.evidence: Store key is user_id. practices/tips.md User ID Management: one app user can map to many Memobase users so two roleplay agents do not share memory. Character vs user vs relationship are not typed tables.
identity_split.label: measured

silence.evidence: Default context template: Unless the user has relevant queries, do not actively mention these memories. That is a prompt instruction, not a trauma/kink/spoiler gate. only_topics can drop slots at retrieve.
silence.label: measured

poisoning.evidence: profile_validate_mode filters meaningless LLM extracts and checks slot descriptions. Not a jailbreak or persona-trust filter. Inserted blob text is otherwise trusted.
poisoning.label: measured

forgetting.evidence: DELETE /users/profile/{user_id}/{profile_id}, delete event, delete user, delete blob. No documented decay. Forget-that is an app call, not an NLP verb.
forgetting.label: measured

cost_shape.evidence: docs/cost.md: retrieve is precompiled profile, not per-turn extract. Insert buffers then batch LLM. Event embedding optional (enable_event_embedding). Slot count and max_pre_profile_token_size bound prompt tokens. They claim about 5x cheaper and faster than mem0 on that page.
cost_shape.label: measured

local.evidence: Apache-2.0. Self-host via src/server. Cloud at api.memobase.dev is optional. Needs an LLM and optional embedder.
local.label: measured

mcp.evidence: docs/templates/mcp.md: first-party server in memobase/src/mcp with save_memory, search_memories, get_user_profiles.
mcp.label: measured

companion_fit_reason: Structured user profiles plus event timeline and a retrieve-nothing prompt line. Still one user_id bag unless the app splits ids. No character autobiography, no silence beyond a template sentence, eval is cost vs mem0 not companion behavior.

published_eval.name: Memobase vs mem0 cost/speed comparison on docs/cost.md
published_eval.claimed_score: about 5x cheaper and 5x faster than mem0
published_eval.what_it_actually_scores: Vendor cost and latency vs mem0, plus a quality slogan (gist vs structured profile). Not LoCoMo-style fact QA and not companion silence/identity.

open_unknowns: Exact merge rule when two slot values conflict (overwrite vs keep both) in server source was not opened after GitHub rate-limit.
Named public QA bench numbers were not found on the docs index.
